name: Ollama
description: Get up and running with Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.2, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, Gemma and other models.
editorialSummary: The most popular way to run open models locally: a simple CLI and desktop app with an OpenAI-compatible API. Pull models by name, chat in the terminal, and point any local UI at localhost.
whyCare: Default local runtime for hobbyists and teams—huge model library, minimal setup, and the ecosystem hub that Open WebUI, LibreChat, and coding tools already speak.

name: Open WebUI
description: User-friendly AI Interface (Supports Ollama, OpenAI API, ...)
editorialSummary: Polished ChatGPT-style web UI for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible backends, with RAG, tools/MCP, multi-user auth, and rich admin controls. The default frontend for many self-hosted stacks.
whyCare: Turns a local model server into a full product experience—documents, agents, and team access—without building your own chat app.
notes: GitHub license is NOASSERTION; project uses a custom Open WebUI License (BSD-like with branding restrictions). Source-available; verify license for your deployment size.

name: NextChat
description: ✨ Light and Fast AI Assistant. Support: Web | iOS | MacOS | Android |  Linux | Windows
editorialSummary: Lightweight cross-platform ChatGPT-style client (web + Tauri desktop) with broad provider support including Ollama. Fast to deploy on Vercel or self-host.
whyCare: Huge adoption and a simple path to a portable multi-provider chat client when you want less stack than LibreChat or Open WebUI.

name: GPT4All
description: GPT4All: Run Local LLMs on Any Device. Open-source and available for commercial use.
editorialSummary: Early mainstream desktop app for local LLMs on CPU-friendly hardware, with a curated model catalog and commercial-friendly MIT licensing. Historically important onboarding path for offline chat.
whyCare: Still a recognizable brand for “ChatGPT offline,” especially when you want a simple installable client rather than a Docker stack.
notes: Last push May 2025 as of verification; treat as historically significant but check activity before depending on it for new stacks.

name: AnythingLLM
description: Stop renting your intelligence. Own it with AnythingLLM. Everything you need for a powerful local-first agent experience
editorialSummary: All-in-one local-first workspace: chat, document RAG, agents, and multi-user modes with desktop and Docker installs. Strong productization of private AI for individuals and small teams.
whyCare: One package for docs + chat + agents without assembling Open WebUI, a vector DB, and glue scripts yourself.

name: LocalAI
description: LocalAI is the open-source AI engine. Run any model - LLMs, vision, voice, image, video - on any hardware. No GPU required.
editorialSummary: Drop-in OpenAI-compatible API gateway that runs LLMs, vision, audio, and image models locally—including CPU-only paths. A self-hosted alternative when you want one engine for multimodal workloads.
whyCare: Closest OSS “OpenAI API at home” for mixed modalities without locking into a single vendor runtime.

name: textgen
description: Open-source desktop app for local LLMs. Text, vision, tool-calling, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. 100% private.
editorialSummary: Successor to text-generation-webui: a private desktop app for local LLMs with vision, tool-calling, and OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs. Long-standing power-user favorite for local experimentation.
whyCare: Deep local control—loaders, extensions lineage, and API compatibility—when browser UIs feel too opinionated.
notes: Repository renamed from oobabooga/text-generation-webui to oobabooga/textgen.

name: Jan
description: Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer.
editorialSummary: Open-source ChatGPT alternative that runs fully offline as a desktop app (Tauri), with local model management and optional remote providers. Strong focus on privacy-first everyday use.
whyCare: Best “download and chat offline” experience for users who want a native app rather than Docker/Ollama + browser UI.
notes: GitHub license field is NOASSERTION; LICENSE file states Apache-2.0.

name: LibreChat
description: Enhanced ChatGPT Clone: Features Agents, MCP, Skills, DeepSeek, Anthropic, AWS, OpenAI, Responses API, Azure, Groq, o1, GPT-5, Mistral, OpenRouter, Vertex AI, Gemini, Artifacts, AI model switching, message search, Code Interpreter, langchain, DALL-E-3, OpenAPI Actions, Functions, Secure Multi-User Auth, Presets, open-source for self-hosting. Active
editorialSummary: Feature-rich self-hosted ChatGPT clone with multi-provider routing, agents, MCP, artifacts, and serious multi-user auth. Suited to teams that need one portal across cloud and local endpoints.
whyCare: Enterprise-leaning self-host chat platform when Open WebUI’s Ollama-first story isn’t enough and you need auth, agents, and many providers.
notes: GitHub /releases/latest 404 (recent releases marked prerelease); latestRelease taken from newest published tag v0.8.7.

name: Chatbox
editorialSummary: Cross-platform desktop/mobile AI client with multi-provider support including Ollama. Emphasizes a polished client UX for daily chatting across local and cloud models.
whyCare: Strong alternative to browser UIs when you want a native client that still talks to local OpenAI-compatible servers.

name: Khoj
description: Your AI second brain. Self-hostable. Get answers from the web or your docs. Build custom agents, schedule automations, do deep research. Turn any online or local LLM into your personal, autonomous AI (gpt, claude, gemini, llama, qwen, mistral). Get started - free.
editorialSummary: Self-hostable “AI second brain” with chat over personal docs and the web, custom agents, automations, and local/cloud LLM backends. Strong Obsidian/Emacs-friendly personal knowledge angle.
whyCare: Goes beyond a chat shell into personal knowledge + automation while staying self-hostable and local-LLM friendly.

name: Vane
description: Vane is an AI-powered answering engine.
editorialSummary: Self-hosted AI answering/search engine (formerly Perplexica) built around local or remote LLMs plus search backends like SearXNG. Privacy-oriented alternative to cloud answer engines.
whyCare: If your “local AI stack” needs web-grounded Q&A—not just chat—this is the go-to OSS Perplexity-style stack.
notes: Renamed from Perplexica (ItzCrazyKns/Perplexica → ItzCrazyKns/Vane). localOfflineCapable false because search grounding typically needs network/SearXNG.

name: SillyTavern
editorialSummary: Power-user LLM frontend focused on character chat, lorebooks, extensions, and deep prompt control. Connects to many local backends (KoboldCPP, textgen, Ollama, etc.).
whyCare: The standard UI for roleplay and highly customized local chat workflows that generic ChatGPT clones don’t cover.

name: llamafile
description: Distribute and run LLMs with a single file.
editorialSummary: Mozilla’s single-file LLM distribution format: ship a GGUF model as one executable that runs across platforms. Ideal for portable demos and air-gapped sharing.
whyCare: Simplest possible distribution story—“download one file, run the model”—without installing a full local stack.
notes: GitHub license field is NOASSERTION; LICENSE header states Apache 2.0 (project also documents additional notices).

name: WebLLM
editorialSummary: High-performance in-browser LLM engine via WebGPU—no server required. Brings local inference into the browser tab for demos and privacy-sensitive web apps.
whyCare: Unique local-AI deployment target: client-side models without installing Ollama or Docker.

name: KoboldCpp
description: Run GGUF models easily with a KoboldAI UI. One File. Zero Install.
editorialSummary: One-file GGUF runner with a KoboldAI-compatible UI and API—zero-install local inference popular with SillyTavern users. Emphasizes easy binaries over complex server setups.
whyCare: Fastest path from a GGUF download to a usable local backend for creative/roleplay frontends.

name: chat-ui
description: The open source codebase powering HuggingChat
editorialSummary: Open-source SvelteKit chat UI that powers HuggingChat; self-hostable against Hugging Face Inference and compatible backends. Clean reference implementation for a production chat front door.
whyCare: Battle-tested UI from Hugging Face if you want to self-host a HuggingChat-like experience with your own endpoints.
